learning.title: Do not pass a function as a string to locator.evaluate in a spec
learning.trigger: A Playwright spec reads a value from the page with locator.evaluate and the code runs only against a live stack, so no fixture run exercises it.
learning.mistake: The M1 journey called target.evaluate("(element) => element.closest('label')?.textContent ?? ''"). A string is evaluated as an expression, so the arrow function was never called and the result was undefined; the first live run died on undefined.trim() after a paid coordinator turn.
learning.rule: Read page values with locators (for example locator("xpath=ancestor::label").textContent()) or pass a real function. A static unit test over the spec source rejects the string-function form, because a live-only spec cannot be run by the rails.

verification.requirement: tests/unit/m1-journey-spec_test.ts fails when a spec or helper passes an arrow function to evaluate as a string.
